title: AGENTS.md
text: sketchpad lightweight, p5.js-inspired drawing system generative art, built S7 classes grid graphics. bypasses ggplot2 entirely: small set drawable shapes (shape_circle, shape_blob, shape_ribbon, shape_twist, shape_bezier) expose computed points property, composed sketch, rendered draw(). shared foundation extracted author’s personal generative-art sketchbook (sketches repo) intended depended various series-* generative art project repos.

title: AGENTS.md
text: section documents package works today. design rationale behind choices, rejected alternatives, record API got , see .agents/HISTORY.md.

title: AGENTS.md
text: style – container color/fill/linewidth/linetype/ linejoin, forwarded grid::gpar(). fill accepts either plain colour string output fill_*() helper (see “fill_*() texture family” ); default fill_solid("black") (.e. "black"). linetype (default "solid", forwarded lty) linejoin (default "round", validated one "round"/ "mitre"/"bevel") independently re-validated beyond linejoin’s enum check – linetype accepts anything grid::gpar()’s lty (named types, integer codes, custom hex dash string) validation left grid draw time. lineend/ linemitre deliberately yet exposed – see .agents/PLAN.md. point_set – polygon’s vertices (x/y numeric vectors, equal length). Named point_set rather points exported constructor doesn’t mask graphics::points(); every drawable’s points property (see ) still called points, since property isn’t top-level exported name can’t mask anything. drawable – parent class every shape. Declares three properties: style (default style()), geometry (validated string, one "polygon"/"path"/"points", default "polygon" – tells draw() grob type build, dimensional reading: "points" 0D, "path" 1D, "polygon" 2D value current shape_*() constructor uses), computed points property subclasses override. meant instantiated directly. drawable’s constructor sets geometry’s default explicitly (argument default, just new_property(default = ...) spec) bypasses S7’s auto-generated constructor – see “Gotchas”. shape_raw – trivial drawable: x/y supplied directly points. Usually produced convert(), constructed hand. shape_circle – centroid + radius + n (point count); points n evenly-spaced points around circumference. shape_blob – like shape_circle, radius perturbed simplex noise (ambient::fracture()/ambient::gen_simplex()/ ambient::fbm()), giving irregular outline. range controls noise amplitude, frequency/octaves/seed control noise field. shape_ribbon – tapered band (x, y) (xend, yend), width modulated simplex noise sqrt taper goes zero ends. shape_twist – like shape_ribbon, underlying path smoothed Brownian bridge (built directly stats::rnorm() via internal smooth_bridge() helper – longer dependency e1071::rbridge(), reproduces bit--bit seed) rather straight line. shape_bezier – outline follows Bezier curve arbitrary number control points (x/y), evaluated via Bernstein polynomial basis (internal bernstein() helper, De Casteljau’s algorithm). Ported series-lissajous, redesigned: original bare S7_object producing curve data frame, consumed internally separate bezier_ribbon drawable. shape_bezier parent = drawable, ’s directly usable draw() – cost always rendering closed polygon (curve’s last point connects straight back first), since every drawable’s points drawn grid::polygonGrob(). open/stroked-curve option. bezier_ribbon ported; see PLAN.md. sketch – list drawables (shapes property). Built sketch() + shape_circle() + shape_blob(...); + method requires S7 method registration, S3 `+.sketch` (see “Gotchas”). draw() – S7 generic, dispatch_args = "object". Methods drawable (single shape) sketch (renders every shape one shared, equal-aspect viewport); catch-method class_any warns returns invisible(NULL) anything else. xlim/ylim default range object’s points. methods build grob via internal geometry_grob() helper (R/draw.R), switches drawable’s geometry property: grid::polygonGrob() "polygon", grid::polylineGrob() "path", grid::pointsGrob() "points" – style@fill omitted gpar() latter two, since closed polygon interior fill. style@linetype/style@linejoin forwarded gpar() stroked geometries ("polygon", "path") "points", line dash join. convert() – S7’s generic (defined package); method(convert, list(drawable, shape_raw)) “freezes” drawable’s computed points plain shape_raw, preserving style. constructor functions concrete drawables share shape_* prefix (shape_circle(), shape_blob(), shape_ribbon(), shape_twist(), shape_bezier(), trivial shape_raw()), mirroring fill_*() family – groups “produces drawable polygon” functions one discoverable, greppable prefix distinct fill_*(), draw(), convert() families.

title: AGENTS.md
text: Every drawable drawn single grid::polygonGrob() inside grid::viewport() equal-axis scaling (width/height set via "snpc" units 1:1 aspect ratio preserved regardless device’s aspect ratio). draw(sketch) computes one shared viewport/axis-range across every shape’s points, draws shape’s polygon list order – later shapes drawn top. draw() needs special-casing pattern/gradient fills: grid::gpar(fill = ...) already accepts colour string "GridPattern"-inheriting object interchangeably, object@style@fill passed straight either way.

title: AGENTS.md
text: R/fill.R holds sixteen fill_*() constructors style@fill: fill_solid() (validated colour string, grid::pattern() involved), fill_none() (thin fill_solid(NA_character_) wrapper – NA already valid, transparent grid::gpar() colour, wrapper reads clearly call site; note still renders closed unfilled outline, since every drawable currently draws closed grid::polygonGrob() – see “Deferred: open/stroked curve support” .agents/PLAN.md), fill_hatch()/fill_crosshatch() (diagonal hatching, sharing tile-shape technique – see ), fill_checker() (two-colour checkerboard), fill_stripe() (solid alternating bands via self-repeating hard-stop grid::linearGradient(), tile repetition), fill_stipple()/fill_scatter()/fill_halftone() (scattered dots / arbitrary drawables / randomised-radius dots, seeded via withr::with_seed() like shape_blob()’s noise – see “Known rendering risk” fill_stipple()’s docs), fill_scribble() (wandering lines built random integer-frequency sine harmonics via internal scribble_lines() helper – periodic construction, tiles seam; direction fixed "horizontal" "vertical" , arbitrary angle – see “Known limitation” docs section), fill_noise() (rasterised ambient simplex/fractal field, sampled torus seamless tiling), fill_marble()/fill_flow() (variants fill_noise() sharing internal torus_grid()/torus_noise() helpers: fill_marble() displaces sinusoidal bands torus-periodic turbulence veined look; fill_flow() domain-warps final field’s tile angles second, seed-decorrelated torus-periodic field swirlier, curl-noise-like look – share fill_noise()’s occasional faint tile-boundary rasterization seam, visible since sin()/warping amplify small mismatches), fill_image() (caller-supplied raster, letterboxed default preserve pixel aspect ratio), fill_gradient() (linear/radial via grid::linearGradient()/radialGradient()), fill_vignette() (colour faded via grid::.mask() alpha mask – helper using masks). fill_solid() return object grid::pattern(), sharing base S3 class "GridPattern". unifying design constraint across : grid::pattern() tiles sized fraction target polygon’s bounding box, fixed physical square, every helper takes aspect argument (target’s bounding-box width/height ratio) correct – computed via internal bbox_aspect() helper. Two different corrections needed depending ’s drawn: Directional content must tile seamlessly (fill_hatch()/ fill_crosshatch()) draws plain corner--corner diagonal controls rendered angle via tile’s width/height ratio (internal hatch_tile_dims() helper) – never via raw direction vector baked segment’s coordinates. extend = "repeat" translates tile copies whole tile-widths/heights, slope exactly 1 (corner--corner) leaves visible mismatch every tile edge. Content periodicity constraint (fill_stipple()’s dots, fill_gradient(), fill_vignette()’s mask) instead makes tile physically square (height = spacing * aspect), content drawn plain "npc" inside needs correction. Shared argument validation lives internal validate_fill_args() (spacing/aspect, optional angle check via angle = NULL).

what: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: sketchpad lightweight, p5.js-inspired drawing system generative art, built S7 classes grid graphics. provides small set drawable shapes (shape_circle(), shape_blob(), shape_ribbon(), shape_twist()) can composed sketch() rendered draw().

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: can install development version sketchpad GitHub :
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("djnavarro/sketchpad")

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: shape_blob() circle whose radius perturbed simplex noise. six blobs arranged around ring, one per colour:
code: library(sketchpad)  values <- tibble::tibble(   x = cos(seq(0, pi * 5 / 3, length.out = 6)),   y = sin(seq(0, pi * 5 / 3, length.out = 6)),   n = 500L,   fill = c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088"),   color = fill ) blobs <- purrr::pmap(values, shape_blob) blobs |> sketch() |> draw()

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: Randomising position, radius, noise range many blobs gives organic composition:
code: set.seed(3) palette <- c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088") n_blobs <- 200L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_blobs, sd = 1.5),   y = rnorm(n_blobs, sd = 1.5),   n = 500L,   fill = sample(palette, n_blobs, replace = TRUE),   radius = runif(n_blobs),   range = runif(n_blobs, min = 0, max = .5),   color = fill ) blobs <- purrr::pmap(values, shape_blob) blobs |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: shape_ribbon() tapered, noise-displaced band drawn two points:
code: set.seed(3) palette <- c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088") n_ribbons <- 200L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_ribbons, sd = 1.5),   y = rnorm(n_ribbons, sd = 1.5),   xend = x + 1,   yend = y,   width = 1,   n = 500L,   fill = sample(palette, n_ribbons, replace = TRUE),   color = fill ) ribbons <- purrr::pmap(values, shape_ribbon) ribbons |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: shape_twist() like ribbon, follows Brownian bridge instead straight line, giving wandering, twisted appearance:
code: set.seed(1) palette <- c("#de9151", "#f34213", "#2e2e3a", "#bc5d2e", "#bbb8b2") n_twists <- 400L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_twists, sd = 2),   y = rnorm(n_twists, sd = 2),   xend = x + 1,   yend = y + rnorm(n_twists, sd = 1),   width = runif(n_twists, min = .1, max = .3),   smooth = 6L,   n = 100L,   fill = sample(palette, n_twists, replace = TRUE),   color = fill ) twists <- purrr::pmap(values, shape_twist) twists |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: Checkerboard pattern fill — fill_checker
text: fill_checker() builds grid::pattern() fill value renders two-colour checkerboard. cheapest member hatch family build: checkerboard square direction way hatch line (compare fill_hatch()'s corner--corner diagonal, needed specifically tile sloped line seamlessly), tile content just four plain quadrant rectangles – two-colour-grid special case fill_crosshatch() already falls back angle multiple 90 degrees, pulled helper.

code: fill_checker(   color1 = "black",   color2 = "white",   spacing = 0.2,   aspect = 1,   extend = "repeat" )

title: Checkerboard pattern fill — fill_checker
text: color1, color2 two checker colours. Defaults "black" "white". spacing Baseline tile size, fraction target's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 0.2. aspect Width--height ratio target polygon's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 1 (square bounding box). extend Passed grid::pattern(). Default "repeat".

title: Checkerboard pattern fill — fill_checker
text: pattern object returned grid::pattern(), suitable use fill argument grid::gpar().

title: Checkerboard pattern fill — fill_checker
text: fill_*() helpers, grid::pattern() tiles sized fraction target polygon's bounding box rather fixed physical square, checker squares render rectangles, squares, non-square bounding box. Pass target's width--height ratio aspect correct – tile- squaring technique fill_stipple() uses dots – default aspect = 1 exact square bounding box.

title: Crosshatch pattern fill — fill_crosshatch
text: fill_crosshatch() builds grid::pattern() fill value renders two mirror-symmetric hatch lines, angle -angle, forming "X" inside tile. shares fill_hatch()'s tile-shape technique: lines drawn two corner--corner diagonals single rectangular tile (rather arbitrary baked-slope), tile seamlessly extend = "repeat", tile's width/height ratio – diagonals' coordinates – determines rendered angle. See fill_hatch()'s details matters.

code: fill_crosshatch(   color = "black",   angle = 45,   spacing = 0.1,   aspect = 1,   linewidth = 1,   extend = "repeat" )

title: Crosshatch pattern fill — fill_crosshatch
text: color Line colour. Default "black". angle Hatch angle degrees, measured counterclockwise positive x-axis. Default 45. spacing Baseline tile size, fraction target's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 0.1. aspect Width--height ratio target polygon's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 1 (square bounding box). linewidth Line width. Must positive number. Default 1. extend Passed grid::pattern(). Default "repeat".

title: Crosshatch pattern fill — fill_crosshatch
text: pattern object returned grid::pattern(), suitable use fill argument grid::gpar().

title: Crosshatch pattern fill — fill_crosshatch
text: lines share one tile shape, perpendicular angle = 45 (classic crosshatch look); angles two lines symmetric horizontal axis right angles . Genuinely perpendicular hatching arbitrary angle need two differently-shaped tiles layered separate fills, function attempt. angle multiple 90 degrees, two mirrored diagonals coincide, case handled separately drawing horizontal line vertical line instead (simple grid).

title: Domain-warped noise texture fill — fill_flow
text: fill_flow() swirlier variant fill_noise(): sampling final noise field, tile's (theta_u, theta_v) angles (see fill_noise() details angles, raw (u, v)) displaced second, independent torus-periodic noise field – "fBm fBm" domain-warping recipe popularized flowing, curl-noise-like textures, adapted warp field torus-periodic rather sampled directly, keeping whole result seamless.

title: Domain-warped noise texture fill — fill_flow
code: fill_flow(   color = "black",   spacing = 0.5,   aspect = 1,   resolution = 32L,   alpha = 1,   warp = 2,   warp_frequency = 1,   warp_octaves = 1L,   frequency = 1,   octaves = 2L,   seed = 1L,   extend = "repeat" )

title: Domain-warped noise texture fill — fill_flow
text: color Fill colour. Default "black". spacing Baseline tile size, fraction target's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 0.5. aspect Width--height ratio target polygon's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 1 (square bounding box). resolution Raster resolution (pixels per tile edge). Must positive integer least 2L. Default 32L. alpha Maximum opacity, noise field's peak. Must number (0, 1]. Default 1. warp Warp amplitude, radians angular displacement. Must non-negative number. Default 2. warp_frequency Frequency two warp-displacement noise fields. Must non-negative. Default 1. warp_octaves Number octaves warp-displacement noise fields. Must positive integer. Default 1L. frequency Noise frequency, shape_blob(). Must non-negative. Default 1. octaves Number noise octaves, shape_blob(). Must positive integer. Default 2L. seed Integer seed noise field, shape_blob(). Default 1L. extend Passed grid::pattern(). Default "repeat".

title: Domain-warped noise texture fill — fill_flow
text: pattern object returned grid::pattern(), suitable use fill argument grid::gpar().

title: Domain-warped noise texture fill — fill_flow
text: warp field needs decorrelated final field along axis, ambient::gen_simplex()'s 4 input dimensions already fully spent (theta_u, theta_v) torus trick, leaving spare dimension offset. fill_flow() decorrelates seed instead: u- v-displacement fields sampled seed + 104729L seed + 200003L respectively (arbitrary large primes, chosen make collisions user's nearby seed choices unlikely), final field sampled seed . Displacing periodic field's periodic coordinates another periodic field preserves periodicity: shifting u 0 1 still advances theta_u exactly 2 * pi (full turn), warp added end identical since sampled field periodic u – warped angle wraps around exactly unwarped one , seam. fill_noise(), faint tile-boundary rasterization seam can still visible devices despite field exactly periodic (see details); larger warp values tend make noticeable, reason described fill_marble().

title: Gradient fill — fill_gradient
text: fill_gradient() builds grid::pattern() fill value whose tile content single rectangle filled grid::linearGradient() grid::radialGradient(), depending type.

title: Gradient fill — fill_gradient
code: fill_gradient(   colors = c("white", "black"),   type = c("linear", "radial"),   angle = 45,   stops = NULL,   spacing = 1,   aspect = 1,   extend = "pad" )

title: Gradient fill — fill_gradient
text: colors Two colours interpolate . type Either "linear" "radial". Default "linear". angle Gradient direction degrees, type = "linear" (ignored "radial"). Default 45. stops Colour stop positions, numeric vector length colors, NULL space evenly (default used grid::linearGradient()/grid::radialGradient()). Default NULL. spacing Tile size, fraction target's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 1 (one tile spans whole shape). aspect Width--height ratio target polygon's bounding box. Must positive number. Default 1 (square bounding box). extend Passed inner grid::linearGradient()/ grid::radialGradient(), controlling happens beyond colour stops. Default "pad".

title: Gradient fill — fill_gradient
text: pattern object returned grid::pattern(), suitable use fill argument grid::gpar().

title: Gradient fill — fill_gradient
text: Like fill_*() helpers, needs target's bounding-box aspect ratio (aspect) render true rather stretched – correction applied differently . Rather adjusting gradient's coordinates (way fill_hatch() adjusts segment's direction), fill_gradient() corrects tile physically square, exactly fill_stipple() dots: tile square, gradient specified inside plain "npc" needs correction render requested angle, true circle type = "radial". also means gradient tile none fill_hatch()'s periodicity concerns: adjacent tiles simply identical copies square gradient, nothing analogous hatch line's tile-edge dashing avoid. default spacing = 1, one tile spans (, non-square bounding box, slightly overshoots) target's entire bounding box, giving single smooth gradient across whole shape – overshoot invisibly clipped away target's outline. Set spacing < 1 repeating pattern small gradient motifs instead.

text: style container graphical properties passed grid::gpar() drawable object drawn.

title: Graphical style for a drawable object — style
code: style(   color = "black",   fill = "black",   linewidth = 1,   linetype = "solid",   linejoin = "round" )

title: Graphical style for a drawable object — style
text: color Stroke colour. Default "black". fill Fill colour pattern. Either plain colour string, output fill_*() helper – fill_solid(), fill_none(), fill_hatch(), fill_crosshatch(), fill_stipple(), fill_noise(), fill_gradient(), fill_vignette(). Default fill_solid("black") (.e. "black"). linewidth Line width. Default 1. linetype Line dash pattern, forwarded grid::gpar()'s lty. Either named type ("solid", "dashed", "dotted", "dotdash", "longdash", "twodash", "blank"), integer code 0:6, custom hex dash-pattern string (e.g. "13") – see grid::gpar() graphics::par()'s lty full set accepted forms, independently re-validated . Default "solid". linejoin Line join style vertex, forwarded grid::gpar()'s linejoin. One "round", "mitre", "bevel". visible closed shapes , sharp vertices, drawable stroked thick linewidth. Default "round".
